text: Two references naming the same object, so that a change made through one is visible through the other, is called ___ .
explanation: It is usually what you want — an account passed to three subsystems should be the same account, or a deposit recorded by one would be invisible to the others. The trouble is the unintended kind, where a caller believes they hold their own copy. Chapter 20's four places to look are: assignment, passing an argument, returning a field, and storing a reference someone else supplied.
